parsed.restated: (∀ x, ∀ t ≥ 0, derivWithin (fun s => v x s) (Set.Ici 0) t + fderiv ℝ (fun y => v y t) x (v x t) = nu • Laplacian.laplacian (fun y => v y t) x - gradient (fun y => p y t) x + f x t) ∧ (∀ x, ∀ t ≥ 0, divergence (fun y => v y t) x = 0) ∧ (∀ x, v x 0 = u₀ x) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿v) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Ici 0) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿p) (Set.univ ×ˢ Set.Ici 0) ∧ (∀ t ≥ 0, IsOnePeriodic (fun y => v y t)) ∧ (∀ t ≥ 0, IsOnePeriodic (fun y => p y t))
parsed.proof:
constructor
· rintro ⟨⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩, g, h⟩
  exact ⟨a, b, c, d, e, g, h⟩
· rintro ⟨a, b, c, d, e, g, h⟩
  exact ⟨⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩, g, h⟩
parsed.english: For all x and t ≥ 0 the Navier–Stokes equation ∂ₜv + (v·∇)v = ν Δv − ∇p + f holds, with the time derivative taken one-sidedly on [0,∞). The divergence of v(·,t) vanishes for t ≥ 0, and v(·,0) = u₀. Both v and p are C^∞ on ℝⁿ × [0,∞). For every t ≥ 0, v(·,t) and p(·,t) are 1-periodic in each coordinate.
parsed.why_clearer: It flattens the nested `extends` structure into one explicit conjunction of the PDE, incompressibility, initial condition, smoothness and periodicity requirements, and avoids the `Δ` and `ℝ^n` notation.
